Check Whether Periods Can Be Aggregated to a Target Classification

Source: R/period_diagnose_coarsen.R
period_diagnose_coarsen.Rd

Check that observations labelled by labels can be aggregated to the periods in to, without splitting observations, omitting required periods, or counting periods more than once.

period_diagnose_coarsen() reports the results of the checks. period_assert_coarsen() returns labels invisibly if the checks pass, and throws an error otherwise. Neither function recodes the labels or aggregates observations.

Usage

period_diagnose_coarsen(
  labels,
  to,
  include_equals = TRUE,
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent"),
  x_arg = rlang::caller_arg(labels),
  to_arg = rlang::caller_arg(to)
)

period_assert_coarsen(
  labels,
  to,
  include_equals = TRUE,
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent"),
  x_arg = rlang::caller_arg(labels),
  to_arg = rlang::caller_arg(to),
  call = rlang::current_env()
)

Arguments

labels

Vector of period labels.

to

Vector of period labels giving the target classification.

include_equals

Whether to allow identical classifications. Default is TRUE. Set to FALSE to require at least one genuine merge.

interpret_single

How to interpret a label for a single year, such as "2020". Choices are "lower" (the default) and "upper". See below for details.

interpret_multi

How to interpret a label that refers to multiple years, such as "2020-2025". Choices are NULL (the default), "at_upper", and "below_upper". See below for details.

interpret_fail

Action if a label cannot be interpreted: "error" (the default), "warn", or "silent". Uninterpretable labels fail the checks even when parsing errors are suppressed.

x_arg

Name of labels to use in error and warning messages. Defaults to the expression supplied for labels. A function that calls this function can supply its own name, such as "data$age".

to_arg

Name of to to use in error and warning messages. Defaults to the expression supplied for to.

call

Execution environment of the function to name in errors from period_assert_coarsen(). Defaults to the assertion itself. A calling function can supply call = rlang::current_env().

Value

  • period_diagnose_coarsen() returns a list with a logical flag ok and a tibble details, with columns condition, passed, and comment, as in period_diagnose_values(). Checks that depend on earlier failed checks are omitted. Comments give an example of each failure.

  • period_assert_coarsen() returns the original labels invisibly, or raises an error explaining the failures.

Two empty inputs pass when include_equals = TRUE. An empty input paired with a nonempty input fails.

Details

Both inputs must consist of period intervals, with no totals, missing categories, or NA values. Within each input, intervals must not overlap. Repeated labels, and different labels describing the same interval, count as overlapping.

Every source interval must fit wholly inside exactly one target interval. The source intervals assigned to each target must cover it completely, with no gaps. Matching gaps between target intervals are allowed. Use period_assert_values() with no_gap = TRUE if continuous coverage is also required.

By default, identical classifications pass. Equality is based on intervals, regardless of spelling or ordering. With include_equals = FALSE, at least one target interval must combine two or more source intervals; other intervals may stay unchanged.

The same interpretation rules apply to labels and to. Unlike period_coarsen_to(), these functions also check for overlaps among source observations and for complete coverage of every target. They do not check the values being aggregated or other join keys.

Factors

Both functions check observed values; unused factor levels are ignored. Supply levels(x) explicitly to check all factor levels instead. period_coarsen_to() uses all factor levels when recoding. To coarsen only the values checked here, drop unused levels in both factor inputs, or convert them to character vectors before recoding.

Rules for interpreting inputs

Single-year

Labels for single-year periods sometimes refer to the lower limits of periods, and sometimes refer to upper limits. For instance, the label "2020" is sometimes used to refer to the period that starts at midnight on 1 January 2020 and ends at midnight on 1 January 2021, and is sometimes used to refer to the period that starts at midnight on 1 July 2019 and ends at midnight on 1 July 2020.

The interpret_single argument can be used to distinguish between the two conventions:

interpret_singleRuleExample
"lower""a" -> [a,a+1)"2020" -> [2020,2021)
"upper""a" -> [a-1,a)"2020" -> [2019,2020)

Multi-year

In labels for multi-year periods, the second number is sometimes the upper limit of the period, and sometimes the upper limit minus 1. For instance, the period that starts at midnight on 1 January 2020 and ends at midnight on 1 January 2025 is sometimes labelled "2020-2025" and is sometimes labelled "2020-2024".

The interpret_multi argument can be used to distinguish between the two conventions:

interpret_multiRuleExample
"at_upper""a-b" -> [a,b)"2020-2025" -> [2020,2025)
"below_upper""a-b" -> [a,b+1)"2020-2024" -> [2020,2025)

If interpret_multi is NULL (the default), then multi-year labels are interpreted using the "at_upper" convention. If, however, the "at_upper" convention leads to intervals with widths 4, 9, 14, ..., then agetime emits a message. Supplying an explicit value for interpret_multi silences this message.

Open

A period that is open on the left has no lower limit, and a period that is open on the right has no upper limit. Labels for open periods are not affected by interpret_single or interpret_multi.

Some examples of open periods:

LabelInterval
"<2000", "before 2000", "under 2000"(-Inf,2000)
"2000 or earlier", "up to 2000"(-Inf,2001)
"2000+", "2000 or more", "2000 or later"[2000,Inf)

Labels starting with "-", such as "-2000", are not accepted.

See also

  • period_coarsen_to(), period_mapping(), period_assert_values()

  • age_assert_coarsen(), age_diagnose_coarsen()

  • cohort_assert_coarsen(), cohort_diagnose_coarsen()

Examples

labels <- c("2000-2005", "2005-2010", "2010+")
target <- c("2000-2010", "2010+")
period_assert_coarsen(labels, to = target)
period_coarsen_to(labels, to = target)
#> [1] 2000-2010 2000-2010 2010+    
#> Levels: 2000-2010 2010+

## equality is allowed by default
period_assert_coarsen(target, to = target)
period_diagnose_coarsen(target, to = target, include_equals = FALSE)
#> $ok
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $details
#> # A tibble: 7 × 3
#>   condition         passed comment                                              
#>   <chr>             <lgl>  <chr>                                                
#> 1 labels_intervals  TRUE   NA                                                   
#> 2 to_intervals      TRUE   NA                                                   
#> 3 labels_no_overlap TRUE   NA                                                   
#> 4 to_no_overlap     TRUE   NA                                                   
#> 5 contained         TRUE   NA                                                   
#> 6 complete          TRUE   NA                                                   
#> 7 not_equal         FALSE  Source and target describe the same classification; …
#> 

## missing years in a target interval
period_diagnose_coarsen(c("2000-2005", "2010+"), to = target)
#> $ok
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $details
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   condition         passed comment                                              
#>   <chr>             <lgl>  <chr>                                                
#> 1 labels_intervals  TRUE    NA                                                  
#> 2 to_intervals      TRUE    NA                                                  
#> 3 labels_no_overlap TRUE    NA                                                  
#> 4 to_no_overlap     TRUE    NA                                                  
#> 5 contained         TRUE    NA                                                  
#> 6 complete          FALSE  "Target '2000-2010' in 'target' is not fully covered…
#> 

## an open interval on the left can also be coarsened
period_assert_coarsen(c("<2000", "2000-2005"), to = "<2005")

## specify inclusive upper endpoints for multi-year labels
period_assert_coarsen(
  c("2000-2004", "2005-2009"),
  to = "2000-2009",
  interpret_multi = "below_upper"
)
